image.alt: Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve has a loop, enters from the top right, goes down steeply to the left, almost linearly, approaches the x-axis, concave up, passes through a point labeled (15, 2), touches the positive x-axis at a point close to the origin, briefly crosses the y-axis twice as it goes up to the left turns and then goes up to the right, gradually, almost linearly but slightly concave down, and exits at the right of the viewing window.

Details A curve is drawn within a square. The top left, bottom left, and bottom right corners of the square are labeled 13, 0, and 13, respectively. The curve has many loops and slopes upward to the right from the bottom left corner of the square to its top right. The curve is symmetric about the diagonal connecting the top left and bottom right corners. The first half of the curve is as follows: The curve begins at the bottom left corner, traces a thin loop, oriented along the diagonal of the square, followed by an arch bulging up and to the left, with its right leg tracing another broader loop, goes up and down reaching a sharp low point, and then goes up reaching a sharp high point, traces a similar broad loop as before but inverted, and then traces a thin loop now oriented toward the bottom left corner of the square. The second half of the curve is a mirror image of the first part as it proceeds up and to the right.

exercises.instruction: 79, 80, 81, 82, and 83 Curvature The curvature at a point $$P$$ of a curve is defined as $$\kappa = \left| \frac{d\phi}{ds} \right|$$ where $$\phi$$ is the angle of inclination of the tangent line at $$P$$ , as shown in the figure. Thus the curvature is the absolute value of the rate of change of $$\phi$$ with respect to arc length. It can be regarded as a measure of the rate of change of direction of the curve at $$P$$ and will be studied in greater detail in Chapter 13. Details A curve and a line are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve resembles a part of a circle, enters from the left, goes down to the right, crosses the positive y-axis, reaches a low point, goes up to the right, and exits at the top right of the viewing window. A point is marked on the curve near its exit point and is labeled P. The line enters from the bottom of the viewing window, slopes upward to the right at an angle phi from the positive x-axis, crosses the positive x-axis, exits at the top right of the viewing window, and is tangent to the curve at P.
